title: oncall-scratchpad-mar-04-2026
content:
2026-03-04 Oncall scratchpad - Jordan Kim

Summary of overnight pages:
- 03:15 UTC - high 5xx rate on hosted-api (INC-4521). Root cause: downstream cache eviction + model node OOMs after batch-size change. Paging: me, Mia.
- 04:07 UTC - failover to backup region succeeded, traffic shifted in ~45s.
- 06:30 UTC - small regression in latency after rollback; still monitoring.

Immediate follow-ups (today):
1) Post-incident actions (P1):
   - Create incident timeline + collect traces (assigned to me) -> include top 10 noisy request ids and traces. (JIRA-INC-4521)
   - Capture model node memory profiles and bump oom-kill threshold in staging. (TODO: run memprof script on canary)
   - Revert the batching config change in dedicated pool (was applied at 02:50 UTC). Confirmed rollback at 03:50 UTC. Add additional safety guard to CI.

2) Runbook TODOs (short term):
   - [ ] Update "hosted-api 5xx" runbook with the new cache eviction checks (lines to add: redis eviction metrics, cache hit ratio thresholds).
   - [ ] Add explicit step to triage batch size changes: who approves, which canary window to use.
   - [ ] Add quick commands for forcing failover and rollback to runbook (examples below).

Quick commands (notes for runbook)
- Check error rate: kubectl -n hosted-api logs deploy/proxy --since=2h | grep "5.." | wc -l
- Verify model node OOMs: kubectl -n models describe pod <pod> | grep -i oom
- Failover traffic: curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/failover?region=eu-west-1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
- Rollback batching config: kubectl -n serving apply -f /configs/batching/previous-config.yaml

3) Monitoring/alerts tweaks (low effort):
   - Add an alert for cache eviction rate > 0.2% sustained 5m. (Owner: Mia)
   - Add runbook link to the alert description.

4) Communication
   - Drafted a short status update for customers (sent at 08:15 UTC). Copy saved in #incident-updates slack thread (link above). Need to paste into CS ticket for impacted accounts. (Owner: Ethan)

Notes / Observations:
- The model-side memory spike correlated with a sudden increase in input sequence length from a customer load test. Need to add sequence-length caps per route.
- Autoscaler did not scale fast enough for the model pool because the HPA target was still using custom metric that had a 1m scrape delay. Consider switching to node-level metrics or reduce scrape interval.

Followups for weekly retro:
- Discuss safer rollout guardrails for batching/quantization changes (proposal: mandatory canary with synthetic workload + smoke test that runs for 30m).
- Evaluate whether KV cache TTL defaults should be increased for high-mem models.

Personal TODOs (today):
- [ ] Finish incident timeline and attach traces to INC-4521 (due EOD).
- [ ] Open runbook PR with commands and eviction checks (PR draft: runbooks#78).
- [ ] Sync with infra (15:30 PT) about HPA scrape interval change.

Things to ask in handover:
- Did any customers see data leakage? (checked logs quickly, no evidence, but confirm with CS)
- Were there any recurrent errors from the same client IPs? (Ethan to check)

Misc notes / scratch:
- Memory profiling snippet I used: python tools/memprof.py --pod <pod> --duration 60 --output /tmp/memprof.json
- Approx cost impact estimate: ~3 hours of degraded latency across 2000 rps peak -> rough extra tokens estimate ~120M tokens cost bump. Will include estimate in postmortem.

Slack/links to paste in postmortem:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CG1234567/p1677912345000500
- Runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/78
- Incident ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-4521

Notes-to-self: keep runbook changes minimal and tested in staging before merging. If adding new alerts, add low-noise threshold first and iterate.
